transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. It's just gotten to the point where I felt like I really needed to talk to someone about it.
Have you also been feeling sad, hopeless, or disconnected from things that usually bring you pleasure, or is the main issue just the lack of energy?

It’s definitely more than just a lack of energy; these past few weeks it feels like a gray cloud has settled in and I just feel hollow and hopeless. I’ve completely lost interest in things I normally love, like fishing and gardening, and even the simplest tasks feel like I'm wading through deep mud.

How long have you been experiencing this feeling of hopelessness and loss of interest in activities, is it something that's been going on for a few weeks, months, or has it been coming and going over a longer period?

This low, hopeless feeling has actually been hanging over me since late last year, so I've been stuck in this depression for about eleven months now with only brief breaks. These overall cycles of ups and downs have been going on off and on for about a year, but it's really come to a head over this past month.
Can you tell me more about these brief breaks you've had from the depressive feelings, were they spontaneous or triggered by something, and how long did they typically last?

Those breaks are actually phases where I feel the exact opposite—really revved up, full of energy, and on top of the world for about a week or so. They seem to just happen on their own as part of a cycle rather than being triggered by anything specific. They've just become a lot more noticeable and disruptive over this past year.
During these high-energy phases, have you ever found yourself engaging in impulsive or risky behaviors, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or impulsive decisions?

Yeah, during that last up spell, I went on a big online shopping kick and ordered a bunch of extra networking gear and smart home gadgets we didn't really need or budget for. I kept telling myself it would pay off in the long run, but I ended up putting way more on our credit card than was smart.

Did these episodes of increased energy and impulsivity, like the recent shopping spree, significantly impair your social or occupational functioning, or were they more of a nuisance but still manageable in your daily life?

During those high-energy periods, I actually felt incredibly productive and wired, so they felt manageable at the time, even though I did get snappy with people and overspent on my credit card. The severe impairment—like getting written up at work and withdrawing from my family—actually happens during my low periods, not the high ones.

Have you ever had a high-energy episode that was severe enough to require hospitalization or cause significant problems in your relationships or at work, rather than just being a period of heightened productivity and impulsivity?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized for those high-energy times. While I did some impulsive things like overspending on credit cards, sending late-night work emails, and getting snappy when questioned, they didn't cause severe disruptions. The major problems, like getting a formal warning at work and pulling away from my family, only happen when I crash into these low, drained periods.

Can you estimate how many of these high-energy episodes you've experienced over the past year, and did any of them last longer than a few weeks or cause significant distress to you or those around you?

I’ve had a few of these high-energy phases off and on over the past year, and they usually only last about a week or so, never more than a couple of weeks. While they aren't long-lasting, they do cause some distress and tension, like when I get snappy with people who question my ideas or overspend on our credit cards. However, the most severe disruptions still happen during my low periods.

You've mentioned these high-energy episodes typically last about a week or so, but have you ever experienced any that lasted longer, say more than two weeks, which might have significantly impacted your daily functioning or relationships?

No, they've never lasted that long; those high-energy phases usually only run for about a week at most. They've never stretched out to two weeks or caused a major breakdown in my daily life while they were happening. The severe disruptions and problems with my work and family really only happen when I crash back down into the low periods.

Can you clarify if there have been any periods where you felt completely normal, without either the high-energy symptoms or the depressive symptoms, lasting for at least two months, within the past year?

No, I haven't had any long stretches of feeling normal like that over the past year. For about the last eleven months, I've felt stuck in some level of depression, and the only breaks I've had are those brief, high-energy bursts rather than any real time of feeling balanced.
Can you confirm whether these cycles of high and low periods have been consistent over the past year, or have there been any changes in their frequency, duration, or severity over time?

They’ve been happening off and on for about a year, but they have really come into focus and felt much more disruptive over this past month. For most of the last eleven months, I've just felt stuck in this low, depressed state, with only those brief, revved-up bursts breaking it up. It feels like the impact of these cycles is getting heavier.

Have you experienced any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks without any intervening high-energy episodes, and if so, how did those episodes compare in severity to your current state?

Yes, my low periods last much longer than two weeks; I feel like I've been stuck in this depression for most of the past eleven months with only those brief, high-energy breaks. This current low stretch over the past month has been much more severe and harder to handle than before. It's actually the worst it's been, especially since it led to that formal warning at work.
Can you describe the shortest and longest duration of your depressive episodes over the past year, and how often these episodes have occurred, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?

The longest depressive episode is definitely this current one, which has been hanging over me for most of the past eleven months, only interrupted by those brief, week-long high bursts. Before this, the low periods would typically last a few weeks at a time. These cycles of crashing into these drained stretches have been happening off and on for about a year now.

Can you estimate the total number of days or weeks you've spent in these high-energy episodes versus the low, depressive episodes over the past year to help understand the balance between these states?

The low, depressive periods have taken up the vast majority of the past year, leaving me feeling stuck in a depression for about eleven months. In contrast, the high-energy, revved-up episodes only last for about a week or so at a time before I crash back down. It's really been mostly low periods with just a few brief high weeks mixed in.

Have you experienced at least four episodes of some type of extreme mood episode, either high or low, within the past 12 months, which is necessary for distinguishing between the potential diagnoses we are considering?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact count of those episodes over the past year. These ups and downs have been happening off and on for about a year now, but I haven't kept track of the specific number of times they've switched.
Can you try to approximate or recall roughly how many times you've switched between these high-energy and low, depressive states over the past year, even if it's not an exact count?

It hasn't really been a constant, rapid switching back and forth. Instead, it's been one long, continuous stretch of feeling low for about eleven months, interrupted by just a few brief, intense bursts of high energy. These cycles have been happening off and on for about a year, but they've really come into focus over this past month.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced at least four distinct episodes of either depression or high-energy episodes within the past 12 months, which would help clarify the nature of your condition?

Honestly, I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of distinct episodes. It's hard to count them precisely because the low feelings have felt almost continuous over the past year, with only those brief breaks of high energy.

Can you try to recall if there have been at least four distinct episodes where you switched between feeling extremely high or extremely low within the past 12 months, to help us better understand your condition?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of times it has happened, as I haven't kept a precise count of the shifts. I just know that these ups and downs have been happening off and on for about a year now.

Can you think of any specific events, dates, or periods that might help you or me estimate how many times you've switched between these high-energy and low, depressive states over the past year, even if it's not an exact count?

The clearest switch was about a month ago, when I had that high-energy week of staying up late working on projects and then immediately crashed into this current low period that led to my work warning. Other than that, I’ve just felt stuck in some level of depression since late last year, only interrupted by a couple of other brief, revved-up bursts. These cycles have been happening off and on for about a year, but it's mostly just been that one long low period with those few quick peaks.

Can you think back over the past year and try to estimate or recall roughly how many distinct episodes of either high energy or depression you've experienced, even if you can't pinpoint exact dates or durations, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?

Over the past year, these cycles of highs and lows have been happening off and on. I've felt stuck in a low, depressed state for most of the past eleven months, but that long stretch has been broken up by brief, week-long bursts where I suddenly feel overly revved up and high-energy.
Can you try to recall or estimate the total number of distinct episodes, either high-energy or depressive, you've experienced over the past year, to help us differentiate between potential diagnoses?

It is really hard to give you an exact count of distinct episodes. Over the past year, I have mostly felt stuck in a low, depressed state for about eleven months, which has been interrupted off and on by a few brief, week-long bursts of being highly revved up and energetic.

Have you experienced any periods within the past year where you had at least four distinct episodes of either depression or high-energy episodes, regardless of their duration, to help us better understand the pattern of your symptoms?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of times this has happened or if it has been at least four distinct times. I just know that these ups and downs have been happening off and on over the past year.

Can you look back over the past year and try to identify at least four specific times when you switched from a high-energy state to a low, depressive state or vice versa, to help clarify the pattern of your symptoms?

I can't really pinpoint four specific dates or times because these cycles tend to blur together. I just know I've been dealing with these general ups and downs off and on for about a year, mostly feeling depressed with only those brief bursts of high energy.

Can you consider your entire year and estimate if you've had at least four distinct episodes where you clearly switched between feeling extremely high or extremely low, regardless of how long each episode lasted?

I'm not quite sure about the exact number of times I've switched back and forth over the year, or whether it has been at least four distinct times. I haven't kept a precise count of the cycles, so I can't really give you a definitive number.
Have you ever experienced any symptoms of mania, such as excessive spending, reckless behavior, or decreased need for sleep, during your high-energy episodes?

Yes, during those high-energy periods I'd only sleep three or four hours a night but wake up feeling completely wired, convinced I didn't need any more rest. I also went on that big online shopping spree where I put a bunch of expensive networking gear and smart home gadgets on our credit cards, even though we hadn't budgeted for them.
During your high-energy episodes, have you ever experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions?
No, I have never experienced anything like hallucinations or delusions during those high-energy periods. Even when I'm really revved up, I still have a clear grasp on reality.
Have you ever experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during either your high-energy or low, depressive episodes?

No, I have never experienced anything like hallucinations, hearing voices, or delusions during either my high or low periods. My mind has always remained clear in that regard, even when my mood is swinging.
Can you confirm if the total duration of your high-energy episodes, when combined, accounts for less than half of the total time you've spent in either high or low episodes over the past year?

Yes, that's absolutely correct. The low, drained periods have lasted for the vast majority of the past year, about eleven months in total. The high-energy bursts only last for a week or so at a time, so they make up a much smaller portion of the overall time.

Considering your high-energy episodes typically last about a week and your depressive episodes can last several weeks to months, do you think the pattern of these episodes meets the criteria where the depressive episodes significantly outnumber the high-energy episodes in terms of total duration over the past year?

Yes, absolutely. The depressive periods definitely dominate the timeline, since I've felt stuck in that low, drained state for most of the past eleven months. The high-energy bursts only seem to last for about a week or so at a time before I crash right back down.

Can you confirm that the total number of days spent in depressive episodes is significantly greater than the total number of days spent in high-energy episodes over the past year, which might help differentiate between potential diagnoses like F31.4, F31.5, F31.6, F31.7, F31.8, and F31.9?

Yes, I can definitely confirm that. I've been stuck in a low, depressed mood for most of the past eleven months, while those high-energy, revved-up periods only last for about a week or so at a time. The amount of time I've spent in the low phases is much, much greater.
